title: Comparative latency slicer for model routes (stream vs sync) with multi-window SLIs
creator: Asha Menon
description: Build a single comparative dashboard that lets operators slice p50/p95/p99 latency by model and route, comparing streaming vs non-streaming IO modes across multiple rolling windows (1m, 5m, 1h, 24h). This is intended to provide fast anomaly hunting for regressions introduced by runtime changes (batching, kernel selection, KV cache), and to serve as the canonical SLI visualization for paging rotations and post-incident RCA. The board must include fast links to traces for sample slow requests, an ability to filter by model_variant, customer_tier, region, and a histogram/quantile distribution panel per selection. Key constraints: keep dashboard query latency under 500ms; avoid high-cardinality ad-hoc queries by pre-aggregating percentile series where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for selected model route and compares 'stream' vs 'sync' side-by-side for 1m/5m/1h/24h windows
Each percentile point links to a sample set of traces filtered to that percentile and IO mode
Percentile computation uses streaming-friendly aggregators (t-digest-based pre-aggregation) to bound memory and query time
Query templates and pre-aggregation jobs are in place and do not increase ingestion cost by >10%
Documentation page with query examples, how to interpret SLI drift, and runbook steps is published
tech_design: Telemetry changes: add explicit tag 'io_mode' with values 'stream'|'sync' at the serving ingress; propagate trace_id into streaming adapters and ensure trace sampling is consistent. Metric naming: latency.raw_ms (histogram buckets) and latency.tdigest (t-digest summaries) with labels: model, model_variant, route, region, customer_tier, pod_role. Percentiles computed by query engine using precomputed t-digest rollups at 1m granularity and a 5s rollup for 1m window to support low-latency dashboards. Chosen aggregator: t-digest for better accuracy at p99 with lower memory than naive HDR. Dashboard backend: Grafana+ClickHouse (existing metrics store) with a small materialized view that stores per-route, per-io_mode tdigest blobs. Traces: link generation uses trace-search with query params (trace_id hint from slow_sampleer). Avoid adding new high-cardinality label combinations; use label cardinality caps and sampling for low-volume customers.
implementation_steps: 1) Telemetry: add io_mode tag to ingest path + update streaming adapters to propagate trace_id (ENG-87620 draft)
2) Metrics: implement ClickHouse materialized view for per-route tdigest aggregates (1m rollup)
3) Queries: author Grafana query templates for p50/p95/p99 across multiple windows (1m/5m/1h/24h) and verify performance
4) Traces: wire dashboard panels to trace-search to load representative traces for selected percentile and IO mode
5) QA: run load test with synthetic traffic (different models/routes) to verify dashboard latency and correctness
6) Documentation & runbook: add KB that explains how SLI thresholds map to alerts and suggested mitigations
7) Rollout: staged rollout behind feature flag with canary teams (internal + two customers)
8) Post-rollout: collect feedback and iterate on panel layouts and filters
testing_plan: Unit tests for t-digest rollup job and serialization/deserialization of blobs
Integration test to ensure io_mode tag present end-to-end and trace links resolve to sampled traces
Performance test: dashboard query p50/p95/p99 under 500ms at production traffic sample (10k routes simulated)
Accuracy test: compare tdigest percentiles vs raw histogram for a set of synthetic distributions to confirm p99 error < 3%
rollout_plan: Enable behind 'latency_slicer' feature flag. Phase 1: internal-only (engineering + SRE) for 48h. Phase 2: enable for monitoring team and two pilot customers for 1 week. Phase 3: global enable if no regression in dashboard latency or backend cost. For any significant SLI drift detected after rollout, automatically roll back t-digest materialization and revert to aggregated histograms and alert the on-call.
